source: BBOC 2025 Big Ten Season Preview Part 1+2 (Stuckey/Collin Wilson)

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Penn State, Michigan and Oregon; HOSTS Ohio State (7th game, at home before a bye). Five Big Ten home games; only plays one team off a bye (Purdue). Tricky road spot at Purdue (off bye) between USC and Ohio State; road game at Indiana Sept 20. Seven straight games to open before the bye.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts effectively PASS/UNDER-lean; neither will bet it (Stuckey 'I'm out,' Collin 'pass on a win total'). Popular sleeper Stuckey sells hard: went 5-1 in one-possession games and had freakishly good injury luck (whole OL and Altmyer started all year), the 8 teams beaten went a combined 42-66, and hasn't won 8+ in back-to-back years since 1990. QB Altmyer certainty (21 TD/5 INT) but he collapsed vs elite secondaries/pressure (1 BTT, 6 TWP vs Oregon & Penn State). WR is the worry - lost Bryant & Franklin to NFL, only returnees Beaty & Dixon are slot guys, no true outside/deep threat. All five OL back but Stuckey thinks overrated. Defense returns nearly everyone but was horrific vs the run (127th rush success, 132nd line yards) and did nothing to fix it. Collin makes it 8.3 (mkt 7.5 over -160) and wants to FADE Belima as a road dog - he's 12-4 ATS as road underdog and gets motivated by doubt. Stuckey 7.7. Pass on the total; live upset spot vs Indiana.

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Michigan and Ohio State but goes to Penn State, Iowa and Oregon (three tough road games). Only four conference road games, mostly soft (Purdue, Maryland). Seven games projected double-digit favorites. Only ONE bye all year (oddly placed before the Nov 28 Purdue game). Late spots at Maryland (could be a corpse/fired coach) and Wisconsin (could be fired coach) plus Purdue to close.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts OVER and both showed value. Signetti year two; last year 12-1, +15 turnovers but beat only one winning team (Michigan) and wins came vs teams combined 51-81 - yet they demolished them, which matters. QB Fernando Mendoza in from Cal (16-6 TD/INT but 12 BTT to 17 TWP); Collin's deep dive found his accuracy is NOT the issue (Cal 14th on-target, same TWP rate clean vs pressured), so the TWP look like fixable youth. Backfield still good (Hemby from Maryland, BB from UAB, Black back); WR duo Sarratt & Cooper/Williams return (15 receiving TDs). OL has questions (lost center + RT) but added Coogan from Notre Dame (26 career starts) at center. Loaded the portal on the DL (Wyatt, Daily, Wheeler, Ratcliff) - Stuckey 'nailed the portal.' Defense finished 5th in havoc (classic JMU/Signetti); CB DeAngelo Pollins 10 PBUs. Collin 8.79, Stuckey 9.1. The surprise-team dark horse; road slate may block a Big Ten title trip.

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Michigan AND Ohio State; gets Indiana, Oregon and Penn State all AT HOME (Kinnick). Five Big Ten home games. Schedule gets tougher: plays 5 of the top 7 and none of the bottom 4 (had 7 of bottom 8 last year). Two free wins vs UMass and Albany at home. Almost all the coin-flip games are on the road (Iowa State, Rutgers, Indiana, Wisconsin, USC, Nebraska).
teams.key_injury: QB Gronowski missed spring game (injury) but healthy and practicing in camp
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT: Collin OVER (7.3, over 6.5 -170, prefers alt 7), Stuckey lower (6-6.5) but NOT going under. HIGH VARIANCE - Stuckey has nine single-digit projected spreads, four under three; nearly every game winnable or losable. QB Mark Gronowski transfers from South Dakota State (93 TD/20 INT over four years, low 2% TWP) - potentially their best QB since Stanzi, but FCS-to-FBS translation is the disagreement between the hosts (returning-passing-yards mirage). WRs all back but nobody's had a 500-yard season since 2019. OL is the real question - Collin hates the interior; RB Kamari Multo (3.6 YAC) will have to create his own yards like Kaleb Johnson did (Iowa was 80th in line yards). DL might be the best in the Big Ten (six of eight in two-deep return). Special teams elite as always; will steal a game or two. Parker's D should bounce back but LB super inexperienced and CBs Lee/Hall must improve. Ferentz 30-16 ATS on the road last 10 years (~66%). Collin taking the over; Stuckey passing.

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Oregon, Ohio State and Penn State; HOSTS Michigan. Five Big Ten road games (one at Ford Field vs Michigan State). Should start 3-0 (FAU, NIU, Tulsa at home). Winnable middle: at Wisconsin, host Washington, host Nebraska, at UCLA.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT-ish: Collin UNDER (3.9), Stuckey nothing/PASS (4.1). Three-way QB battle - true freshman Malik Washington (No.5 in 2025 class) dealing with injuries, Justin Martin (UCLA transfer) won the spring, Locksley won't name a starter until the Sunday before the FAU opener. Outside top 100 in returning production, only a handful of returning starters. Classic Maryland: always good pass-catchers (added Ferruque, Webb, TE Fleming; Smith back) but the OL is a perennial disaster - projected tackles from Central Connecticut State and Shorter. Defense gutted: of the nine best defenders, ONE returns (S Husky); lost five to the NFL. New coordinators; NIL drama last year and the team quit/didn't like each other. Finished 127th havoc-allowed on O, 129th quality drives, DEAD LAST in coverage, 131st-134th in multiple categories. New DC Ted Monachino wants edge havoc but finished 125th last year with an inexperienced depth chart. Very hard to power-rate; true-freshman-QB variance. Collin under, Stuckey pass.

teams.key_avoids: THE EASIEST Big Ten schedule in the conference (outside top 50 SOS). Avoids Penn State AND Oregon; HOSTS Ohio State to end the year. Five Big Ten road trips (Nebraska, USC, Michigan State, Northwestern at Wrigley, Maryland) but projected ~three-TD favorite in a four-game October 25-Nov 22 stretch. Non-con at Oklahoma is the toughest defense they'll see (both expect a loss). Tricky game 11 at Maryland before Ohio State.
teams.key_injury: S Rob Moore health to watch
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT - the sharpest disagreement of the preview. Collin LOVES the schedule ('easiest thing you could pull in the Big Ten'), sees 8-1/7-2 conference floor and bets Michigan +380 to MAKE the Big Ten championship (not win it). Stuckey CAN'T get there - projects an 8-4 team (8.5 wins), sees losses at Nebraska, at USC, Ohio State plus likely Oklahoma, thinks they're a year away. QB freshman Bryce Underwood (over Mikey Keene) - even if bad he beats last year's 129 pass yds/game, zero 40+ completions, dead-last explosive passing. New OC Chip Lindsey (really a QB coach/caretaker). RBs good (Marshall, Haynes from Alabama). Weapons thin - loss of TE Loveland huge, WR room 'meh.' OL a big worry, especially the inexperienced right side (Opabi, Striegel). Defense strong (edge Moore/Guy, LBs Hausman/Barham, CBs Barry/Hill 70 combined PBUs) though interior DL drops off after losing Grant/Graham. Wink Martindale D held up fine (1st pass rush, 26th havoc). Lottery ticket on Underwood; Collin's title-game longshot vs Stuckey's under.

teams.key_avoids: Only THREE Big Ten home games in Spartan Stadium and Michigan & Penn State are two of them - so only two vs the bottom seven. Maryland game is at Ford Field to close. No easy road games (at USC, at Nebraska, at Indiana, at Minnesota, at Iowa). Swing game is Boston College week two at home. Gets Minnesota late (worse than early).
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts UNDER (Stuckey 5.73, Collin makes them +3 / going under 5.5 +115). Year two of Jonathan Smith and his coordinators; top-20 returning production. QB Aidan Chiles must improve (13 big-time throws, 20 TWP) but was pressured on 42% of dropbacks (bottom 10) behind awful tackles - Collin says 'scrap the numbers' given 143 pressures. RB room worse (Tolliver from Sac State, only 2.8 YAC, not Skattebo). WR Nick Marsh is a stud (2.1 YPRR) and the connection Chiles needs. OL lost its top two interior to the NFL; only the (bad) tackles return - transfers must hit. Both safeties (Spencer, Martinez) back; D was good tackling/run defense (21st rush success) but 99th havoc, 129th pass rush, six straight games without a sack. Collin's angle: if the OL/pass-blocking and DL pressure show up in the box early (Western Michigan, BC), the power rating could jump 5 points and wipe out the preseason numbers - but until then, under. Stuckey trusts Smith to a bowl but not a talented roster; going under.

teams.key_avoids: Five Big Ten home games; road losses projected at Ohio State, Iowa and Oregon. Likely wins Buffalo(?), Northwestern (State), Purdue at home. Six coin-flip games where they're favored in five but by less than a field goal in four. Opens week one vs Buffalo - both hosts eyeing Buffalo as a live week-one play (even outright).
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts UNDER (Stuckey 6.25 'under under under,' Collin under 7 +115). Major QB downgrade - Brosmer to the Vikings, now redshirt-freshman Drake Lindsey with little depth behind him (Pryor transferred out). Lose 80% of last year's targets (Jackson & Spencer); transfers Coleman/Louis/Tracy are a drop-off in a Harbaugh scheme that asks a lot of the QB. OL loses LT Ersery, LG Cooper, RT Carroll (100+ combined Big Ten starts) - five players at new positions and Collin RIPS the 55 transfer 'starts' as '55 shitty starts' (Marshall 160th, Ray 525th among guards per PFF). D loses both DEs, both CBs and the nickel to the NFL; safety group good but CB room way down, was 111th in line yards last year (worst in 15 years). 10 players lost to the NFL, six on D; third DC in three years. FADE candidate. Collin's actual angle: Buffalo (Pete Lembo, strong MAC trench) beating Minnesota outright week one. Both under.

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Oregon and Ohio State; five Big Ten home games. Opens vs Cincinnati in Kansas City (technically neutral). Hosts Michigan (Sept 20 - Collin's game-of-the-year play, Michigan -3.5, thinks it should be -6.5). Lots of winnable games.
teams.bboc_notes: No explicit win-total lean stated (market number not cited on the pod). Matt Rhule year three - his previous stops produced 11 and 10 wins in year three. But Nebraska is 1-5 in one-possession games last year, 10-35 in one-score games since 2018 (35 one-score losses, 10 more than anyone), 0-27 vs ranked in last 27, 0-8 in OT since 2018 (outscored 39-0, -20 yards). QB Dylan Raiola must take the leap (4 TD/9 INT over last eight games) but Collin notes solid freshman marks (17 BTT to 12 TWP, 4.7% TWP under pressure) pointing to a bigger year two; OL returns 130+ starts, added WR Dane Key (2.5 YPRR at Kentucky). New OC Dana Holgorsen (full offseason) seen as an upgrade over Satterfield. THE question is the DEFENSE - lost top five DL to the NFL/portal, lost the DC and DL coach; new DC John Butler installs a 3-3-5 with an inexperienced front and transfer LBs. Experienced secondary may not benefit without the pass rush. Special teams (disaster last year, bottom-10) looks fixed with new coordinator/punter. Variance team; Collin fading them via Michigan -3.5.

teams.key_avoids: Not much travel overall - boxed in geographically (only real trip is week one at Tulane, plus at USC). Five Big Ten home games but three are on the lakefront and two at Wrigley. First five manageable (at Tulane, Western Illinois, UCLA, ULM at home). Then at Penn State (loss). Beat only Maryland and Purdue in Big Ten play last year.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT on the power rating: Collin OVER (4.4, leans over), Stuckey couldn't find four wins and is lower ('over or nothing,' harder to get there). QB Preston Stone in from SMU - Collin loves him, thinks he's finally healthy; must be his 2023 self (33 BTT, 13 TWP). WR is the big question - lost both top receivers (one to NFL); pieces are Stanford & South Dakota State transfers (basically 'South Dakota State East'). Griffin Wild a multipurpose slot/out tool (3.2 YPRR). Top four RBs return (Porter, Himon - nothing special, stability). D should be salty (David Braun) - like the DL, LB Xander Mueller (85 tackles), edge Anto Saka (27 pressures), experienced two-deep secondary (Fussell 5 PBUs), but young/rising DBs. The week-one line vs UCLA short and moving toward Northwestern. Collin bumped them 4-4.5 points from end of last year (hence over four); Stuckey didn't and can't find the wins - the market/SP+ (~12) bump confuses him. Over-or-nothing team.

teams.key_avoids: Preseason favorite to win the Big Ten (+250). Gets Penn State and Texas at home (both losable, likely small favorite). Losable road games at Michigan, at Washington, at Illinois; back-to-back travel to Wisconsin. Rutgers off a bye Nov 22 right before Michigan (bad spot even at -19). ~100th in returning production.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts UNDER 10.5 (juiced -140); Collin also likes NO PLAYOFF (+250) though won't go as far as last year. Defending national champs but a TON of questions. QB BATTLE - Julian Sayin (pure arm, lukewarm camp reviews) vs Lincoln Kienholz (dual-threat) - the style depends on who wins. Lost both RBs in round two (Henderson, Judkins); Peoples/Donaldson (CJ Donaldson from WVU a basher if healthy) a notch down. WR stacked (Jeremiah Smith potential No.1 overall, Carnell Tate, TE Max Klare from Purdue). OL has real questions - new LT Ethan Onenuwa graded 170th at RICE; interior has some playoff experience. The hosts' central concern is COORDINATORS: new OC Brian Hartline (internal) and new DC Matt Patricia are seen as a big downgrade from Chip Kelly and Jim Knowles - Collin docked them two full power-rating points and predicts Patricia 'costs them a game.' Caleb Downs and Jeremiah Smith are the swing stars; 17 lost to the NFL. Ceiling is 10-2; under, and a live no-playoff at plus money.

teams.key_avoids: Avoids Ohio State and Michigan. Hardest game is at Penn State (both call it a loss and a very tough early spot - Penn State off a bye, having shown nothing in a cupcake non-con, vs Lanning's bag of tricks). Good early runway (Montana State, Oklahoma State, at Northwestern, Oregon State) to sort the QB. Other tough spots: at Iowa (off bye), USC at home, cross-country at Rutgers (watch the noon-ET kickoff Oct 18), at Washington to close. Four of six mid-year opponents come off byes.
teams.key_injury: WR Evan Stewart injured, likely out for the year
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts UNDER 10.5 (unders taking a ton of money); this is a deliberate FADE for Stuckey ('we're gonna play Oregon on the under'). Went undefeated last year but 15 players now in the NFL and they don't return much. QB Dante Moore takes over (transfer, one year in system) - Collin's not a believer historically (ugly UCLA pick-sixes) but thinks the Will Stein offense (6-yard average depth of target, like Nix/Gabriel) protects him; 'how many pick-sixes?' is the over/under. Whole offense new except C. NEAR-DISQUALIFYING WEAKNESS the hosts hammer: the INTERIOR RUN DEFENSE - undersized DTs (Bear Alexander third team in four years, questionable motivation; Amari Washington 12 tackles in 22 career games), and the schedule is loaded with zone/power-read teams (Penn State, Minnesota, USC, Washington) who can gash them. Edge rush still elite (Uiagalelei 9.5 sacks, Tuioti 5.5). Recruiting top-5, lots of young talent (Dakorien Moore). Both under; interior D the reason.

teams.key_avoids: EASIEST non-conference in FBS (Nevada, FIU, Villanova). Hosts Oregon after a BYE and goes to Ohio State after a BYE - the two hardest games both off byes, huge with Cole Nick/Knowles prep. Out-at-Iowa spot could be tricky (before Ohio State, bye in between). Rest of the schedule very manageable; Michigan State and Nebraska come off byes in November but PSU should be 14-21 point favorites.
teams.key_injury: Some depth concerns (WR and a couple D spots) - injuries the main risk
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts OVER; Stuckey's PICK to win the Big Ten and the No.1 team in the country. Rare Big Ten team with QB CERTAINTY - Drew Allar returns (still must be better vs elite teams and under pressure - footwork/won't throw it away, and nickel Zion Tracy's 39% missed-tackle rate is the one D weakness). Best backfield in the country (Singleton & Allen). Lost top three WRs but added Payne, Hudson (freak), Ross, Pena - an upgrade; TE U reloads (Jenkins). OL mostly back (year two continuity), should take a leap. Year two of OC Andy Kotelnicki plus the huge addition of DC Jim Knowles from Ohio State (who's seen this OSU personnel and beat Will Stein twice) - the hosts call it the best coordinator pairing in college football. Lost Abdul Carter but DL/LB reload (Dennis-Sutton, Durant, Campbell from UNC). Floor is 10 wins, ceiling undefeated. The play the hosts push: NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP futures at 7-8/1 that you tuck away and don't look at until the semifinals - anything short of the CFP semis is a disaster year. Hard over.

teams.key_avoids: Top-15 hardest schedule in the country. Should start 2-0 (Ball State, Southern Illinois at home). Then brutal (USC, at Notre Dame). Best upset spots are catching teams sleeping in good spots: Illinois (comes to Purdue off a bye between USC and Ohio State), Minnesota (hosts Purdue after playing at Ohio State), Rutgers (visits Purdue after hosting Oregon). Then at Michigan, Ohio State, at Washington, Indiana at home to close.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts land ~3 wins on the TOTAL (Stuckey 3.0, Collin 3.2) - No Play on the season total (can't stomach over 2.5 -180). BRAND NEW everything after an absolute disaster last year: new HC Barry Odom, new OC Josh Henson (from USC, air-raid, didn't call plays there), new DC from UNLV. ONE returning starter; could start eleven transfers, ~75 new players, 12 WRs brought in. QB Ryan Browne returns (battle with Malachi Singleton, a runner). HIGH VARIANCE / near-impossible to power-rate - Stuckey admits he could be a full TD/10 points off, cites a Canadian center from Manitoba he has to go watch tape on. Odom's identity: good special teams and a 3-3-5 that SELLS OUT to stop explosives/EPA (roster full of his Arkansas/UNLV 'greatest hits' guys) - so the real actionable angle is UNDERS on Purdue GAME totals early (first-half unders vs Ball State, SIU) before the market catches up. Was 0-3 in one-possession games, -14 turnovers, but does regression even apply when everyone's new? Likely 3-9.

teams.key_avoids: Schedule gets MUCH tougher - gets the top three (plays Oregon, at Ohio State, hosts Penn State to end) after avoiding all of them last year. Five winnable to start (three non-con: Ohio, Miami-OH, Norfolk State; plus Iowa and at Minnesota, both with new QBs) - a chance to start 5-0. Four games out of reach: Oregon, Illinois, Penn State, Ohio State (ceiling 8). 0-40 vs ranked teams since 2009. Ohio State spot is prime (Rutgers off a bye, OSU pre-Michigan).
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts OVER 5.5 - one of Stuckey's summary highlights ('very well-coached'). The handicap: Rutgers was top-5 in havoc allowed, extremely well coached under Schiano/Ciarocca/new-DC Rob Smith, don't make mistakes, and WON FOUR GAMES OUTRIGHT AS AN UNDERDOG last year. QB Athan Kaliakmanis returns (experienced, decent 18-7 TD/INT) but NEAR-DISQUALIFYING accuracy weakness - 123rd in on-target rate, and TWP rate jumps from 1.6% to 5.7% when he sees blitz. RB room down a bit (Monangai to NFL) but Raymond back plus CJ Campbell; WR room Collin likes (Duff, Sheffield from North Texas, Partridge). OL question is the TACKLES - lost NFL LT Pierce, may start a Lafayette transfer at LT. Went transfer-heavy on D (seven of top eight new); like the DL adds (JMU, Weaver) and Henderson from Marshall - coaching-fundamentals numbers (tackling, contested catch) should hold. Collin over 5.5 -125 (6.25), Stuckey 6.5/5.85 (right on market with juice). Trust the staff to six; well-coached over.

teams.key_avoids: Vicious schedule, one of the 10 hardest in the country. Only four Big Ten home games (one road game is at USC). Hosts Penn State, Nebraska, Washington; goes to Ohio State, USC, Indiana, plus road trips to Northwestern and Michigan State (would rather have those home). Only gimmes are New Mexico at home and maybe Maryland (gets Maryland in the second half).
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts UNDER, and both super low - Stuckey projects 4.2, wouldn't be shocked by 3-9. Year two of DeShaun Foster with new OC Tino Sunseri (from Indiana, a power-run/Cignetti guy) - but this was the WRONG year to lean on the portal. QB Nico Iamaleava in from Tennessee - Collin calls it 'one of the worst transfer-portal moves in all of Power Four' (UCLA the only school that met his laughable NIL number); NEAR-DISQUALIFYING QB weakness - zero escapability, 26% pressure-to-sack ratio, only 5 TDs in six games vs winning FBS teams, now behind possibly the worst OL in the Big Ten (hodgepodge journeyman transfers). RBs can't create (Berger declining YAC every stop; nobody over ~3.1 YAC) so it stalls into passing downs and Nico's feet. Defense lost FIVE to the NFL and its top 11 tacklers; secondary entirely portal (Oregon State, Miami, UCF, Ole Miss), no front-seven improvement expected after 114th pass rush, 123rd finishing drives. FADE - Collin's very first app bet was Utah -130 week one vs UCLA. Hard under.

teams.key_avoids: No Penn State, no Ohio State on the schedule. Expects four wins to start before a trip to Illinois; bye week before hosting Michigan. Two remaining coin flips: at Nebraska and hosting Iowa. Softer secondary can be hidden early (Missouri State, Georgia Southern, Purdue, Michigan State to open); Oregon at home is the real test for the DBs. If they beat Michigan at home, a Big Ten championship path opens with only a loss to Oregon.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts high/LIKE it - Stuckey ~8.5, Collin ~8.5, over 7.5 -130. QB Jayden Maiava returns (took over late, more mobile, better Riley fit) - Collin's a 'buyer' (6 BTT vs Notre Dame's all-world secondary). WR duo Makai Lemon (3.3 YPRR, elite) and Jacobi Lane (burner) among the best in the country; RB room still good (Juco Jordan). OL the major question (might start a Purdue transfer at LG; 120th pass blocking) - the one thing that could sink it. The bull case is the DEFENSE: DC D'Anton Lynn's unit made an astronomical rise (from bottom-10 in everything two years ago to 14th PFF tackling, No.1 limiting passing-downs explosives) and added size up front; Collin says Lynn should win the Broyles Award. Eric Gentry a top B1G outside LB, CB Kamari Ramsey a Lynn-system fit; secondary has questions (lost four DBs to NFL) but a soft passing-game schedule hides it. DARK HORSE - Collin holds a 4/1 ticket on USC to make the Big Ten title and likes +750/+2200 (25-1) to win it. Over.

teams.key_avoids: Gets Ohio State, Oregon and Illinois all AT HOME. Plays five teams coming off byes (Ohio State, Maryland, Rutgers, Illinois, Wisconsin). Faces seven of the top ten from last year down to five projected this year - schedule easier than last year. Very little travel - only leaves the time zone about three times (Maryland, Michigan, Wisconsin), plus one California trip for UCLA.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts OVER 7.5 (Collin 8.1, Stuckey ~8, likes it especially at plus money). Year two of Jedd Fisch. QB Demond Williams returns - both hosts LOVE him (8-1 TD/INT, 5-1 as starter over the last two games vs Oregon and Louisville, 'not Sisters of the Poor'); a zone-read problem for defenses. RB Jonah Coleman (67 missed tackles forced on 192 carries, 4.3 YAC) is underrated; Boston back at WR. OL was near dead-last in pass blocking but the losses were all bad players - added Carver Willis (two years RT at Kansas State) at LT, upgrades on the interior; should be much better. New DC Ryan Walters (from the Illinois nasty defenses, replacing Steve Belichick who left with his dad to UNC) - seen as a wash-to-upgrade who adds run-defense balance (Washington was 7th pass success but 117th rush success). DB group still one of the best in the Big Ten (Cario Davis, Price-Hawkins) fitting Walters' cover-one; DL beefed up with P4 transfers. Depth still very young (injury risk) - comes down to Williams' development as a passer. Over.

teams.key_avoids: Roughly the NUMBER-ONE hardest schedule in the country. Only gets one of the projected bottom six (doesn't play Purdue, Northwestern, UCLA, Michigan State or Rutgers - and beat only those three types last year). Plays eight of the projected top 11; on a 2-21 run vs ranked teams. Must start 3-1 (Miami-OH, Middle Tennessee, Maryland at home; loss at Alabama). No breaks after the bye - closing stretch is Michigan, Iowa, Ohio State, at Oregon, Washington, at Indiana, Illinois, at Minnesota.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts OVER (Collin 6.3, Stuckey 5.8, over 5 -140). Top-20 returning production. QB Billy Edwards Jr. in from Maryland - a real fit for new OC Jeff Grimes' RVO ground-and-pound (must play the Jalon Daniels designed-run role), but Fickell hasn't kept a QB healthy in three years and the RBs (Dupree, Jones) are both sub-250, not the classic Wisconsin size - Collin's worry is whether they hold up. Getting back to Wisconsin's identity after the Longo mistake is the story. OL questions at RG and LT (lost both to NFL). The key positive: the FRONT SEVEN got much bigger/deeper (Walker from WMU, Suggs from LSU, Peterson from Tulane) after a historically bad year - DEAD LAST in TFLs, 17 sacks (fewest since 1983), 128th havoc - so the hosts expect big improvement that unlocks the secondary. New DBs a mystery (Forker likely ineligible). HIGH VARIANCE - faces 10 brand-new QBs (2nd most). Fickell and the OLB/ST coach on the hot seat; Grimes was a good hire but the schedule is brutal. Both would play the over if forced.
